name: Electroplating
summary: An electric current puts a thin layer of one metal on a part of another metal. Silver, gold, nickel and chromium plate give a cheap base metal a precious or hard surface.
how: Clean and degrease the base part, then put it in a bath of a salt of the coating metal.
Connect the part to the negative pole and a bar of the coating metal to the positive pole.
Pass a direct current until the layer is 0.5 to 25 µm thick.
Put a copper or nickel under-layer on steel and zinc before a bright top layer.

origin.note: George and Henry Elkington patent cyanide silver plating; Luigi Brugnatelli gilded silver by electrolysis in 1805.

adoptions.via: Elkington silver plate replaces Sheffield plate on factory-made tableware.
Gilt and chrome plate give cast base-metal jewels the look of gold and platinum.
Nickel and chrome plate cover the lamps, the radiator and the bumpers of the car.
Nickel-plated brass and chrome-plated steel become the metal of the modern lamp and chair.
Silver plate and chrome stay on Nordic tableware and lamps next to stainless steel.
